title: Best Tools for Chiefs of Staff (2026)
summary: The best tools for chiefs of staff in 2026, by job: priorities and follow-ups, docs, meeting notes, projects, email, async updates and scheduling.
body_markdown:
The best tools for chiefs of staff aren't the ones with the most features. They're the ones that help you do the job only a chief of staff does: keep the executive team aligned, make sure decisions turn into action, and catch what's slipping before your CEO has to.


That job runs across every tool in the company. Priorities live in docs, decisions get made in meetings, requests arrive in email and Slack, and progress sits in project tools. In a 2025 survey of chiefs of staff run by Notion and Ask a Chief of Staff, calendar, email, project management and to-do lists were the most-used tools.


Below is a practical stack, organized by the job each tool does, with prices checked against each vendor's pricing page in October 2026.


## Key takeaways


-


Build your stack around **jobs, not apps** : priorities and follow-ups, documentation, meetings, projects, email, async updates and scheduling.


-


**BOND** is the layer that connects them, keeping one prioritized list of what needs you and your executive across every tool.


-


Most chiefs of staff can run a strong stack on **six or seven tools** . More than that usually adds noise.

## How we picked the best tools for chiefs of staff


We looked at the jobs that fill a chief of staff's week, then chose the tool we'd recommend for each, judged on:


-


**Fit for the role:** does it help you coordinate across the exec team, not just do individual tasks?


-


**How well it connects:** chiefs of staff work across every system, so integrations matter.


-


**Time to value:** you don't have weeks to configure software.


-


**Price:** verified on each vendor's pricing page.


New to the role? Start with what a chief of staff actually does, then come back to build your stack.


## 1. BOND: priorities, commitments and follow-ups


*A sidekick that manages your to-do list and reminds you when things slip.*


BOND is an AI chief of staff, built for executives and the human chiefs of staff who support them. It connects to Gmail or Outlook, Calendar, Slack, Notion, Linear, Asana, HubSpot, Attio and meeting note tools like Granola, then keeps one self-updating to-do list of what needs attention, ranked P0 to P3.


For a chief of staff, that solves the hardest part of the job: tracking commitments across the whole exec team. Decisions made in the Monday leadership meeting, promises buried in email threads and blockers raised in Slack all land in one place, with what's slipping flagged automatically. BOND learns your priorities over time, so the list stays extremely accurate and cuts through the noise. If you're new to the category, our guide to what an AI chief of staff is covers how it works.


**Key features**


-


Self-updating, prioritized to-do list built from email, Slack, calendar, docs and meeting notes


-


Commitment tracking in both directions: what your exec owes and what they're waiting on


-


A daily morning brief of what's on track, what's slipping and who's waiting


-


Meeting prep and follow-up drafts in your executive's voice


-


Works for individuals and as a shared layer across a leadership team, in Slack and iMessage


**What works:** It replaces the spreadsheet of action items most chiefs of staff maintain by hand, and it catches commitments you'd never have seen.


**Limitations:** It's built for leadership work, not as a general project manager. Keep Asana or a similar tool for detailed project plans.


**Pricing:** Free to start with 10,000 credits. Individual plan is $49/month. Enterprise is custom, with SOC 2 Type II, SSO and SCIM.


**Best for:** Chiefs of staff who own follow-through across the exec team, and founders who don't have a chief of staff yet.


## 2. Notion: docs, wikis and operating cadence


*Where the company's operating system is written down.*


Notion is where many chiefs of staff build the documents that run the company: leadership meeting agendas, decision logs, OKR trackers, onboarding guides and the operating cadence itself. Its databases let you turn a page into a lightweight tracker, and the Business plan adds Notion AI, Notion Agent and AI Meeting Notes.


**What works:** Extremely flexible, widely adopted, and good at becoming the single source of truth for how the company operates.


**Limitations:** Flexibility cuts both ways. Without discipline, a Notion workspace becomes a maze. It also won't tell you what changed or what's slipping unless you go and look.


**Pricing:** Free plan. Plus is $10/seat/month and Business is $20/seat/month (which includes Notion AI). Enterprise is custom. Yearly billing saves up to 20%.


**Best for:** Documenting the operating rhythm, decisions and leadership rituals.


## 3. Granola: meeting notes


*Notes for back-to-back meetings, without a bot.*


Granola captures meetings through your computer's audio, with no bot joining the call, and combines what it hears with the notes you type. After the meeting, it produces enhanced notes, action items and a draft follow-up. It runs on Mac, Windows, iOS and Android.


For a chief of staff, it's a quiet way to capture every leadership meeting and one-on-one without changing how meetings feel. (Here's how to get more out of Granola meeting notes.)


**What works:** High-quality notes, no bot, and chat across all your past meetings.


**Limitations:** Notes live in Granola until you move the action items somewhere else. Connecting it to BOND turns those action items into tracked tasks.


**Pricing:** Free Basic plan with 30 days of meeting history. Business is $14/user/month and Enterprise is $35/user/month.


**Best for:** Capturing decisions and action items from every meeting.


## 4. Asana: cross-functional projects


*Where company initiatives get planned and tracked.*


Asana is one of the most common tools for tracking cross-functional projects and company goals. Chiefs of staff use it to run strategic initiatives, track quarterly priorities across teams and give the CEO a clear view of project status. (If your engineering team lives in Linear, see our guide to Linear for executives.)


**What works:** Good at multi-team projects, with clear owners and timelines, and familiar to most employees.


**Limitations:** Like any project tool, it's only as accurate as the updates people put in. It also can't see the commitments made in email and meetings that never become tasks.


**Pricing:** Free Personal plan for up to 2 users. Starter is $10.99/user/month billed annually ($13.49 monthly). Advanced is $24.99 ($30.49 monthly). Enterprise is custom.


**Best for:** Running company-level initiatives and quarterly priorities.


## 5. Superhuman: email


*For chiefs of staff who live in their inbox.*


Superhuman is a fast email client built around keyboard shortcuts and AI help with writing and triage. For chiefs of staff who handle a high volume of email, often including their executive's, the speed adds up.


**What works:** Getting through a heavy inbox quickly, with AI drafting and organization built in.


**Limitations:** It makes email faster but doesn't connect what's in your inbox to what's happening in Slack, meetings or projects.


**Pricing:** Starter is $25/member/month and Business is $33/member/month, billed annually.


**Best for:** Chiefs of staff and executives with very high email volume.


## 6. Loom: async updates


*Fewer status meetings, more context.*


Loom lets you record quick videos of your screen and yourself, then share them with a link. Chiefs of staff use it for weekly leadership updates, walkthroughs of board decks and context-setting before big decisions, so live meetings can focus on discussion.


**What works:** Replaces status meetings with short updates people can watch on their own time.


**Limitations:** Videos can pile up, and they're hard to skim. Keep them short and pair them with a written summary.


**Pricing:** Free Starter plan (up to 25 videos, 5-minute recordings). Business is $18/user/month and Business + AI is $24/user/month. Annual billing saves up to 17%.


**Best for:** Async updates to leadership and the wider company.


## 7. Calendly: scheduling


*Take scheduling off your plate, and your executive's.*


Calendly handles the back-and-forth of booking meetings with booking pages, round-robin scheduling and routing. It has also started rolling out an AI scheduling assistant.


**What works:** Saves hours of scheduling email, especially for external meetings, candidate interviews and investor calls.


**Limitations:** It schedules meetings but doesn't judge which ones deserve your executive's time. That's still your call.


**Pricing:** Free plan with one event type. Standard is $10/seat/month and Teams is $16/seat/month (billed yearly). Enterprise starts at $15,000 per year.


**Best for:** Chiefs of staff managing external and internal scheduling at volume.


## How to choose your chief of staff stack


Start with the job that's breaking today.


**"Things are slipping between meetings."** Start with BOND, ideally paired with Granola so every meeting's action items are captured and tracked.


**"Nobody knows what the priorities are."** Write them down in Notion and track the big initiatives in Asana.


**"My exec's inbox is out of control."** Superhuman for speed, BOND to surface what actually needs a decision.


**"We have too many meetings."** Move status updates to Loom and let Calendly handle the scheduling.


Then resist adding more. Every new tool is one more place where information can hide. The best stacks are small and well connected. If every request still feels urgent after that, our guide on how to prioritize tasks when everything is P0 can help.


## FAQ


**What are the best tools for chiefs of staff?**


A strong chief of staff stack covers seven jobs: priorities and follow-ups (BOND), docs and operating cadence (Notion), meeting notes (Granola), cross-functional projects (Asana), email (Superhuman), async updates (Loom) and scheduling (Calendly).


**What software do chiefs of staff use most?**


In a 2025 survey of chiefs of staff by Notion and Ask a Chief of Staff, calendar, email, project management and to-do list tools were the most used. Most chiefs of staff build on those and add meeting notes and an AI layer.


**What is the best AI tool for a chief of staff?**


BOND is built specifically as an AI chief of staff. It connects to your email, Slack, calendar, docs and meeting notes and keeps one prioritized list of what needs attention across the exec team. For writing and research, general assistants like ChatGPT or Claude are useful additions.


**How do chiefs of staff track action items across the exec team?**


Capture action items in every meeting with an owner and a date, keep them in one place and review them weekly. Many chiefs of staff now use BOND to pull commitments from meetings, email and Slack into one list automatically.


**Do chiefs of staff need a project management tool?**


Usually, yes, for company-level initiatives. Asana is a common choice. Pair it with a tool like BOND for the commitments that never make it into a project plan.


**How is a chief of staff different from an executive assistant?**


A chief of staff extends the executive's judgment across the company, while an executive assistant manages their calendar, inbox and logistics. Our guide to chief of staff vs. executive assistant covers the difference in detail.
